verses.1: Proverbs of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel.
verses.2: To learn wisdom and discipline, to understand words of insight.
verses.3: To receive discipline of discernment, righteousness, judgment, and equity.
verses.4: To give understanding to the simple, knowledge and discretion to the young.
verses.5: Let the wise listen and grow in learning, and the discerning acquire understanding.
verses.6: To understand a proverb and a figure of speech, the words of the wise and their riddles.
verses.7: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and discipline.
verses.8: Listen, my son, to your father's discipline; do not neglect your mother's instruction.
verses.9: For they are a garland of grace for your head and a chain for your neck.
verses.10: My son, if the wicked entice you, do not consent.
verses.11: If they say, "Come with us, let us lie in wait for blood, let us ambush an innocent man for no reason,
verses.12: we will swallow them alive like the grave, and whole, like those who descend to the pit;
verses.13: we will find all kinds of precious wealth, we will fill our houses with plunder;
verses.14: cast your lot among us; let us all have one purse."
verses.15: My son, do not walk in the way with them, keep your foot from their path.
verses.16: For their feet run to evil, and they hurry to shed blood.
verses.17: For in vain they spread a net where their wings are spread.
verses.18: And they are ready to make themselves guilty, to lie in wait for their own souls.
verses.19: So are the ways of all who do violence; the life of the transgressor is taken.
verses.20: Wisdom calls aloud in the streets, she raises her voice in the broad places;
verses.21: at the head of the noisy streets she cries out; at the entrance of the city gates she declares her words:
verses.22: "How long, you simple ones, will you love being simple? And you scoffers, how long will you scoff? And you fools, how long will you hate knowledge?
verses.23: Turn back to my reproof; behold, I will pour out my spirit to you, I will make my words known to you.
verses.24: Because I called and you refused, I stretched out my hand and no one paid attention;
verses.25: you ignored all my counsel and would not accept my reproof.
verses.26: I too will laugh at your disaster; I will mock when fear comes upon you.
verses.27: When fear comes upon you like a storm, and your distress arrives like a whirlwind, when your troubles come and your calamity descends,
verses.28: then they will call to me, but I will not answer; they will seek me diligently but will not find me.
verses.29: For they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the LORD.
verses.30: They did not want my counsel; they despised all my reproof.
verses.31: Therefore they will eat the fruit of their own way, and be filled with the consequences of their own schemes.
verses.32: For the return of the simple will destroy them, and the ease of the fools will destroy them.
verses.33: But whoever listens to me will dwell securely and be at ease, without fear of evil.

notes:
Notes
- v. 14: "one purse" is a literal translation of "כִּיס אֶחָד" which metaphorically means "shared resources or common wealth."
- v. 32: "the return of the simple" is a translation of "מְשׁוּבַת פְּתָיִם," where "return" is used in the sense of their eventual downfall or reckoning.
- v. 32: "the ease of the fools" is a translation of "שַׁלְוַת כְּסִילִים," where "ease" conveys a false sense of security leading to destruction.
